name: IMON.world
description: Sabbir Hassan Imon's personal site: open-source projects, an interactive pixel world, free browser games, and browser-based coding, AI and system-design learning labs.

serviceWorker.purpose: Offline caching of the site's own static files

site.privacySummary: No analytics, no tracking pixels, no advertising, no fingerprinting and no server-side visitor logging. A small number of free public APIs are contacted directly from the browser, each of which necessarily sees the visitor's IP address.

entryPoints.title: Course catalog
entryPoints.summary: Crawlable lesson links grouped by course and chapter, with links to the three built-in quizzes. All lessons can be opened without an account.

entryPoints.title: IMON | Sabbir Hassan Imon — Learning Labs, Open Source & Pixel Games
entryPoints.description: The main site: open-source projects, a live pixel world with weather, free browser games, daily headlines and a quiz, an interactive world map, and achievements.

sections.title: Learning labs
sections.summary: Browse the coding, electronics and AI courses.

sections.title: Projects
sections.summary: Open-source repositories and what each one does.

sections.title: Pixel world
sections.summary: An illustrated scene with a live weather layer, World Studio controls, a day/night cycle and optional synthesised ambience.

sections.title: Arcade
sections.summary: Free browser games: Snake, Surf, 2048, Ludo, Puzzle, Dev Slots and a racer.

sections.title: Daily
sections.summary: Live technology and science/space headlines plus a daily computer-science quiz.

sections.title: Map
sections.summary: An interactive world map of 18 fictional countries with flags, tied to the Gridworks campaign.

sections.title: Achievements
sections.summary: Badges earned from the games and the labs.

sections.title: About
sections.summary: Who the owner is, the toolkit and the current focus.

entryPoints.title: Code Lab
entryPoints.summary: A browser practice lab for HTML, CSS and JavaScript: lesson panel, file rail, editor, live preview and terminal. Exercises carry a goal, study material, exam instructions and an outcome; correct answers pay XP, wrong answers explain what is wrong, where and how to fix it.

entryPoints.title: AI Lab
entryPoints.summary: Learn Python, machine learning and system design through 54 exercises in five chapters. Python runs in the browser through a small teaching interpreter, with a fake HTTP client and an in-memory SQL engine.

entryPoints.title: Circuits & Signals
entryPoints.summary: Build virtual circuits, change their connections, and inspect signals on a scope.

entryPoints.title: Pixel Arcade
entryPoints.summary: Signal Runner, Prism Breaker and Star Patrol.

entryPoints.title: IMON Gridworks
entryPoints.summary: A standalone 18-city infrastructure management game with a pure simulation engine and a canvas UI. Power and data travel through separate layers; later chapters unlock regional links, LEO ground stations and paid automation.

entryPoints.title: Developer Toolbox
entryPoints.summary: Offline-first developer utilities: JSON/YAML/Terraform/SQL/XML formatters, Base64, JWT decoder, timestamp converter, regex tester, UUID generator, hash generator, colour contrast checker, DNS lookup.

entryPoints.title: Privacy & data notice
entryPoints.summary: Every third-party service the browser contacts, every local storage key, what reaches the optional database on sign-in, and what is never stored.

entryPoints.title: Log in
entryPoints.summary: Optional Google registration and sign-in, account passwords and private cloud progress.

content.generativeAI: not used for page copy; AI-generated artwork is limited to three illustrated landscape backgrounds, and the generation prompts and provenance are published in the repository under docs/art/PROMPTS.md
content.thirdPartyAttribution: Headlines are credited to Hacker News, the Spaceflight News API and DEV Community. Quiz questions come from Open Trivia DB under CC BY-SA 4.0, with attribution travelling with each pack. Weather data is by Open-Meteo. Code Lab lookup results are from Stack Overflow.

interactive.note: Interactive features need a browser. There is no server-side rendering and no page-content API — read the HTML directly.
